question: An analyst has connected her work Google Drive to Claude and asks for last quarter's regional sales file. Claude replies that it cannot find it, although she knows the file exists because a colleague showed it to her. What should she do first?
options: A) Rephrase the request repeatedly until Claude eventually locates the file on the connected drive.
B) Remove the connector and set it up again, as a broken connection is the usual cause of this.
C) Check whether that file is shared with her own account, since the connector uses her own access.
D) Ask her colleague to run the same request and paste his answer back into her conversation.
correct_answers: C) Check whether that file is shared with her own account, since the connector uses her own access.
explanations: Rewording cannot reveal a file the connected account has no permission to open in the first place.
Reconnecting does not widen access, and nothing here suggests the connection itself has failed.
Correct. A connector reaches only what the connecting account can already open, so a file a colleague has not shared with her is simply outside its scope.
This works around the question without establishing whether she is entitled to the file at all.
